recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. The FHIR-core issue was applied historically and then superseded by the THO migration; future national ICD-10-GM URI/OID maintenance should happen through THO or German-affiliate terminology governance rather than by restoring the retired core ICD variants table.
issue_request: FHIR-13123 was a Published/Persuasive Vocabulary change request raised against DSTU2 terminology systems content. It reported incorrect or misaligned ICD-10-GM and ICD-10-NL OIDs, noted that 1.2.276.0.76.5.409 was not a stable all-years ICD-10-GM OID, and asked the FHIR terminology pages to reflect German year-specific terminology/OID practice.
initial_application: The Jira comment cited svn revision 1755. In the git import, d75d919fc1 explicitly applied #13123 by changing the old source/icd.html Germany row from the copied Netherlands OID to a link to the HL7 Germany page and changing the Netherlands row away from the copied German OID; d9bf7e4119 then removed the explicit core icd-10-de URI from that table.
additional_context: Later same-family decisions refined the same ICD area: FHIR-13723 added the German affiliate canonical URL to the old ICD page, FHIR-17771 recorded that ICD-10-NL/DE OIDs were reversed and already fixed, FHIR-35933 intentionally removed the old FHIR-core source/icd.html external-code-system page and moved detailed guidance to THO, and FHIR-41305 corrected the current ICD URI row. Those related issues already have audit commits on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current build-scoped core source in source/terminologies-systems.html lists only generic ICD-9-CM and ICD-10 system identifiers, warns that external terminology content is non-authoritative convenience content, and points to HL7 Terminology for authoritative external code-system information; source/sid-icd-10.html describes only the international ICD-10 system. Current-source searches found no old icd-10-de/icd-10-nl rows or disputed OIDs.
